question.problem:
A store collected data about its profits (in thousands of dollars) for the year's first five months. This data is shown below.

| Month $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit $(y)$ | $12$ | $15$ | $16$ | $15$ | $20$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the profit in the $6$th month, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}78 \\ 250\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
question.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 15 \\ 16 \\ 15 \\ 20\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}78 \\ 250\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10.8 \\ 1.6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=10.8+1.6x.$ 

Finally, to predict the profit in the $6$th month, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =10.8+1.6(6) \\  & =20.4\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the profit in the $6$th month will be $$20\,400.$

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
